tagline.text: An end-of-April festival in Dagupan where over twenty thousand milkfish are grilled in the street

location.label: Location
location.text: Dagupan City, Pangasinan (around City Plaza and downtown roads)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000~3,500 (same-day transport from Manila and meals, rough estimate per person)

children.text: The Bangus Festival is a milkfish festival that Dagupan City, Pangasinan, holds every year in late April. On April 30, tens of thousands of bangus are grilled in the street at Kalutan ed Dalan, followed by the bangus rodeo, street dancing contests and open-air concerts.

Bangus is milkfish, one of the fish Filipinos love most. Dagupan City in Pangasinan is famous for farmed bangus, and the Bangus Festival honoring this fish is held every year from late April to early May. The highlight is Kalutan ed Dalan, the street grilling event on April 30. Long charcoal grills are laid out along a road and the bangus are grilled all at once, an image that has become the symbol of the festival. Bangus is a fish that often reaches Filipino family tables and feels familiar to locals, so many visitors come as families during the festival.

Dagupan's grilled bangus has a close tie to Guinness World Records. According to the records, in 2003 a grill 1,007.56 m long was built on A.B. Fernandez Avenue in Dagupan, surpassing Peru's 613 m record and winning recognition as the world's longest barbecue. The first attempt in 2002 is said to have fizzled out for lack of charcoal, and the city is known to have tried again the following year and succeeded. Some accounts say rain cut the celebration short. Grill lengths and fish counts differ a little between sources, so take the numbers as approximate.

Today's festival is much larger. According to the city government, about 25,000 bangus were grilled at Kalutan ed Dalan on April 30, 2025, which is 5,000 more than the 20,000 of the year before. The Bangusan Street Party held the same day had nine stages, and the city said about one million people watched online and offline combined. After a two-year pause during the pandemic, the festival returned in 2022 and has regained its energy.

The events are not only about grilling. On April 26, City Plaza hosted Gilon Gilon ed Baley, a street dancing contest honoring the fishermen's bangus harvest and the patron saint, John the Evangelist, and on April 28 the Bangus Rodeo judged the heaviest and longest bangus. Dates and programs change a little each year, so check the latest notice from the Dagupan city government before planning. In 2025, events for visitors from the sister city began around April 25, and a flag-raising ceremony took place at City Plaza on April 28. The festival thus runs for nearly a week rather than a single day, so if you arrive a day or two before the grilling you can also see the rodeo and the street dancing contest.

On April 30, long charcoal grills are laid out on downtown roads and the bangus are grilled all at once. In 2025 it was held on the Judge Jose de Venecia Highway Extension and began with a ceremonial lighting of the grills by the mayor and vice mayor. Grilled bangus is said to be available to taste on site, so allow time for the queue. Booths and how food is sold differ each year, so follow the on-site instructions.

That evening, nine concert stages are set up on the road and local and national singers perform. In 2025 it was reported that about one million people watched online and offline combined. The crowd grows as the night goes on, so keep a close eye on your belongings.

A contest to pick the heaviest and longest bangus. In 2025 the heaviest weighed 3.60 kg and the longest was 68 cm, and there were also categories for the prettiest bangus and for the fastest person to sort, debone and eat bangus.

blocks.title: Gilon Gilon ed Baley street dancing

children.text: A dance contest that portrays fishermen harvesting bangus and the patron saint, John the Evangelist. In 2025 teams competed by clusters of villages and Cluster Six won the overall title.

blocks.title: Dagupan old town and City Plaza

children.text: Many official festival events take place around City Plaza. The plaza area is good for getting around on foot, so walk around during the day and watch the shows and booths.
Besides grilling over charcoal, Dagupan's bangus is cooked in many ways, including stuffed bangus (relleno bangus), sinigang and fried bangus. Many people say a plate is relatively affordable.
2025 marked the 25th anniversary of the sister-city relationship between Dagupan and Milpitas, California, so the vice mayor of Milpitas visited the festival. Exchange events change every year.
Dagupan is known for bangus aquaculture. Even outside festival time, you can reportedly see fish farming around the city. Fish farm visits depend on local conditions, so ask in advance.

items.title: Day-trip course
items.subtitle: Leave early in the morning and stay through the evening party

children.text: Board a long-distance bus from Manila to Dagupan. Roads are congested during the festival, so an early start is safer.
Arrive in central Dagupan and start walking from the City Plaza side. Traffic may be controlled in the event zone.
Look around the bangus rodeo or the food booths. Go see the biggest bangus.
For lunch, try grilled bangus or sinigang at a restaurant.
On April 30, head to the Kalutan ed Dalan site and watch the lighting ceremony and the grilling.
Watch the Bangusan Street Party, then head back in time for your bus home.

On event night, buses home tend to be full. Check the last bus time in advance, and if you are late it is safer to stay overnight. The grilling zone is very hot from the charcoal and the crowd. Save your energy in the plaza and in restaurants during the day, and go to the grilling site as the sun starts to set to make it easier.

items.title: 2 days, 1 night
items.subtitle: Arrive the day before and see the morning events

children.text: Arrive in Dagupan the day before the festival and drop your bags at your lodging.
Walk through the city market and plaza to feel the atmosphere.
The next morning, watch the bangus rodeo or the Gilon Gilon dance contest.
From the afternoon, claim a spot in the grilling event zone.
The next morning, buy dried or smoked bangus at the market as a souvenir.
A long-distance bus is the usual way to get from Manila to Dagupan. Travel time and fares vary by company and traffic, so check at the terminal.
During the festival, seats fill up quickly, so line up your tickets both ways in advance.
From the Dagupan terminal into town, take a tricycle or a jeepney.
If you drive, use the expressway toward northern Luzon. On festival days the roads in town are controlled and parking is difficult.
Same-day tours from Manila sometimes appear. Contents and prices differ by operator.
Tricycles are the standard in town, and the fare depends on the distance and on negotiation.
Traffic is controlled around the venues, so follow the instructions and walk when you can.

The Bangus Festival is held from late April to early May, and the Kalutan ed Dalan grilling event is on April 30. In 2025 events continued from around April 25. The schedule changes a little every year, so check the city government's notices.

April and May are the end of the dry season and very hot. Street events can wear you out with sun and heat, so be sure to bring a hat and water, and rest in the shade and in restaurants during the day.

If you miss this period, you cannot see the large-scale street grilling event. You can still taste bangus dishes in Dagupan's restaurants and markets at other times, so if the schedule does not fit, a food trip is another option.

rows: No festival, but good for sightseeing in town.
Festival period. Be ready for the midday heat.

Dagupan has hotels in several grades, but rooms run out early during festival week. Many people also come from nearby cities on the day of the events, so book about a month ahead if possible. Facilities and rates differ by property, so check recent reviews.

Food centers on bangus. You can try bangus grilled over charcoal, stuffed grilled bangus (relleno bangus), the sour soup sinigang and fried bangus. It is a bony fish, so choose a deboned product or be careful when eating. For street grilled food, judge the hygiene with your own eyes.

Bangus seasoned with salt, vinegar and garlic and then grilled has a mild, tender taste. Filipinos often dip it in a sauce of vinegar mixed with soy sauce, calamansi and chili, so try it that way. Even outside festival time, bangus dishes are not hard to find at local restaurants.
Check the Dagupan city government's notices for the exact schedule.
The April 30 grilling event is extremely crowded, so go early to claim a spot and agree on a meeting place with your group.
Bangus has many bones, so be careful when eating it with children.
Bring cash and small change. Market stalls and tricycles are generally cash.
Crowds surge home when the night concert ends. Staying close to the city center is convenient.
Smoke and heat are intense at the grilling site, so people with weak airways should be careful.
For the bangus rodeo, go in the morning to see the big fish up close. In the afternoon the crowds build, so hurry.
Dried bangus (daing) bought as a souvenir smells strong, so bring airtight containers or several layers of plastic bags.
There may be few restrooms near the venues, so use one beforehand while on the move.
Around the grills, charcoal and smoke can be dangerous when taking photos, so shoot from outside the safety line.
Late April is a very hot time of year, and on event days downtown traffic is heavily congested and zones are controlled.
Watch for heatstroke and dehydration, and drink water often.
Pickpockets can appear in the crowds.
Check the city government's notices for traffic-control information in the event zones.
Be careful that bangus bones do not get stuck in your throat.
Traffic home after the events is congested, so leave extra time for the last bus.
If you have a seafood allergy, be sure to check the ingredients when eating festival food.

A famous pilgrimage site of Our Lady in Pangasinan. Travel from Dagupan depends on the transport available, so check.
